findings.reason: Both supplied BFI pages were opened, but neither names Su Li-zhen or explicitly maps that character to Maggie Cheung. They establish the film, Wong Kar-wai, and Cheung in the cast, which is insufficient support for this character-to-actor key and the article's central claim.
findings.required_change: Replace or add a relevant accessible source that explicitly identifies Maggie Cheung as Su Li-zhen, then update source_refs/source_links and recheck this item.

opened_sources.claim_support: Identifies Victoria/Vicky Page as Moira Shearer and gives the film credits.
Supports Shearer's ballet career and role context.
Lists François Truffaut and the principal cast including Jean-Pierre Leaud and Albert Remy.
Explicitly identifies Antoine Doinel as Jean-Pierre Leaud and calls the film Truffaut's directorial debut.
Names Robert Wiene as director; identifies Cesare as the somnambulist and lists Conrad Veidt.
States the 26 February 1920 Berlin premiere, credits Wiene, and explicitly identifies Cesare as Conrad Veidt.
Supports Spike Lee and his character Mookie.
Explicitly describes Lee's Mookie as the pizza-delivery protagonist.
Identifies Deborah Kerr as Sister Clodagh and Kathleen Byron as Sister Ruth.
Names Wong Kar-wai and features Maggie Cheung and Tony Leung; it does not name Su Li-zhen.
Names the director and actors, but does not explicitly map Su Li-zhen to Maggie Cheung.
Supports Claire Denis, Denis Lavant, and the film record.
Explicitly identifies Claire Denis; Denis Lavant as Sergeant Galoup; Michel Subor as Forestier; Gregoire Colin as Sentain; and the Djibouti setting.
